title: Directed colimits of faithfully flat algebras
statement: Let $R$ be a commutative ring, let $I$ be a nonempty directed set, and let $(S_i)_{i\in I}$ be a directed system of commutative $R$-algebras with $R$-algebra transition maps and colimit $S=\varinjlim_i S_i$ [def-weil-pbc-category-colimit]. If each structural map $R\to S_i$ is faithfully flat [def-weil-pbc-faithfully-flat-ring-map], then $R\to S$ is faithfully flat. No injectivity or faithful flatness of the transition maps is assumed.

proof.text: View the algebra diagram as a diagram of R-modules. Package the underlying-module colimit universal property as an IsColimit cocone, then use the filtered-colimit flatness theorem and the unique linear equivalence from the module colimit to the underlying algebra colimit.

source.place: Tag 090N, proof first sentence citing Lemma 05UT (lemma-colimit-flat), lines 9285-9289

proof.text: For a maximal ideal m, faithful flatness gives each stage tensor (R/m) ⊗ S_i nontrivial via the quotient-tensor equivalence. If the colimit tensor were subsingleton, symmetry gives the same for S ⊗ (R/m). The element 1 ⊗ 1 is then zero; the elementwise tensor-colimit theorem carries this vanishing to a later stage. The ring-hom realization of the transition tensor map sends 1 ⊗ 1 to 1, contradicting nontriviality of the later stage tensor.

source.place: Tag 090N, proof middle sentences citing Lemma 00HP and the identification S/mS = colim S_i/mS_i, lines 9290-9298

proof.text: The custom flatness-and-tensor criterion `Module.FaithfullyFlat.of_nontrivial_tensor_quotient` now applies to the flat colimit and the nontrivial tensor products established above.
